Twinet builds and operates a mini-Internet: every student group runs a
real autonomous system with FRR, BGP, OSPF, RPKI and Open vSwitch, spread
across a cluster and graded automatically.

Usage:
  twinet [command]

Available Commands:
  behaviour   Start and stop the scripted perturbations an exercise is built around
  completion  Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  deploy      Deploy the lab, converging whatever is already running
  destroy     Remove every container and overlay object belonging to the lab
  events      Show structured cluster events for a lab
  exec        Run a command in one device or across many
  fault       Inject, verify and resolve network faults
  gateway     Run the SSH gateway students reach their devices through
  grade       Grade student work against a rubric
  graph       Render the topology as a graph
  help        Help about any command
  images      Create and verify reproducible image locks
  incident    Run a reproducible network incident for agent evaluation
  inspect     Show the expanded topology
  msc         Operate a single-worker MSC IPsec/IPsec appliance lab
  node        Inspect and manage the cluster's node agents
  recover     Resume and verify a failed cluster transaction
  restore     Load saved submissions back into a running lab
  runtime     Machine-readable operations for an external evaluation harness
  save        Collect each group's work into a submission archive
  schema      Emit the manifest's JSON Schema, generated from the Go types
  validate    Check a lab manifest and report every problem at once
  version     Print the twinet version
  web         Serve the connectivity matrix and looking glass for a lab

Flags:
  -h, --help                    help for twinet
      --json                    emit machine-readable JSON
  -m, --manifest string         path to the lab manifest or its directory (default ".")
      --runtime string          override the manifest's container runtime for every node (docker, podman, containerd; or set TWINET_RUNTIME)
      --runtime-socket string   endpoint for the overridden runtime (or set TWINET_RUNTIME_SOCKET)
  -v, --verbose                 verbose logging

Use "twinet [command] --help" for more information about a command.
